accepted_examples.german: In weniger als drei Stunden sind wir weg.
accepted_examples.english: We'll be gone in less than three hours.
accepted_examples.note: weniger means less in a direct comparison of quantity or time.

accepted_examples.german: Wie kommt es, dass der Himmel blau ist?
accepted_examples.english: How come the sky is blue?
accepted_examples.note: Himmel refers to the sky in the ordinary weather/space sense.

accepted_examples.german: Laut Tom hat Mary ihr Auto verkauft.
accepted_examples.english: According to Tom, Mary has sold her car.
accepted_examples.note: laut is the preposition meaning according to and introduces the source of a statement.

accepted_examples.german: Es ist wahr, dass die Erde rund ist.
accepted_examples.english: It is true that the earth is round.
accepted_examples.note: Erde refers to the planet Earth in this sentence.

accepted_examples.german: Den Rest des Tages haben wir für uns.
accepted_examples.english: We have the rest of the day to ourselves.
accepted_examples.note: Rest means the remainder of a whole period.

accepted_examples.german: Tom kommt eher aus dem Gefängnis als du.
accepted_examples.english: Tom will get out of prison before you do.
accepted_examples.note: Gefängnis names the prison building or institution.

accepted_examples.english: Your sacrifice was not in vain.
accepted_examples.note: Opfer means a sacrifice in this sentence.

accepted_examples.german: Mein Körper ist nicht so biegsam wie früher.
accepted_examples.english: My body isn't as flexible as it used to be.
accepted_examples.note: Körper refers to a person's physical body; this is a literal example.

accepted_examples.german: Ich werde Sie dem Rest der Besatzung vorstellen.
accepted_examples.english: I'll introduce you to the rest of the crew.
accepted_examples.note: vorstellen means to introduce a person to others.

accepted_examples.german: Wenn du mir hilfst, versuche ich es nochmal.
accepted_examples.english: If you help me, I'll try it again.
accepted_examples.note: nochmal means once again or again in this context.

accepted_examples.german: Diese Wohnung ist größer als alle anderen in diesem Gebäude.
accepted_examples.english: This apartment is bigger than any other one in the building.
accepted_examples.note: Wohnung means an apartment or dwelling in this example.

accepted_examples.german: Er verdient eine halbe Million Yen im Monat.
accepted_examples.english: He earns half a million yen a month.
accepted_examples.note: Million means one million; the quantified amount is explicit.

accepted_examples.german: Du bist in der dritten Klasse, richtig?
accepted_examples.note: Klasse means a school grade or year in this example.

accepted_examples.german: Tom hob die Kiste vorsichtig in die Höhe.
accepted_examples.note: vorsichtig is used adverbially to describe how Tom lifted the box.

accepted_examples.german: Er ist stark genug, um das zu heben.
accepted_examples.english: He's strong enough to lift that.
accepted_examples.note: stark describes physical strength in this sentence.

accepted_examples.german: Es war großartig, mit Tom zu arbeiten.
accepted_examples.english: It was great working with Tom.
accepted_examples.note: Duden classifies großartig as an adjective; here it is predicative after war.

accepted_examples.german: Tom konnte es sich nicht verkneifen zu lachen.
accepted_examples.note: lachen is the infinitive meaning to laugh.

held_examples.german: Je mehr du trinkst, desto weniger ißt du.
held_examples.reason: The sentence uses the superseded spelling ißt; current standard spelling is isst. The other candidate was accepted.

held_examples.german: Die Wolken mag ich am Himmel am meisten.
held_examples.reason: Grammatically possible but less clear and natural for a learner than the direct sky-colour example selected.

held_examples.german: Die Erde ist viel größer als der Mond.
held_examples.reason: Valid, but the selected example provides a short direct statement of the planet sense.

held_examples.german: Tom ist älter als der Rest von uns.

held_examples.german: Tom kommt eher aus dem Gefängnis als ihr.
held_examples.reason: Valid translation variant with the same structure; retained as an alternate rather than the primary learner example.

held_examples.german: Niemand wusste sein Opfer zu schätzen.
held_examples.reason: Valid, but the selected sentence expresses the sacrifice sense more directly and simply.

held_examples.german: Ich bin am ganzen Körper grün und blau.

held_examples.german: Ich werde Sie dem Rest der Crew vorstellen.
held_examples.reason: Near-duplicate of the selected sentence with the synonymous English loanword Crew; keep one primary example.

held_examples.german: Tom probierte nochmal, Marias Aufmerksamkeit zu erregen.
held_examples.reason: Valid but longer and less useful for a first learner example than the short repetition example selected.

held_examples.german: Tom hat eine größere Wohnung als ich.
held_examples.reason: Valid translation is approximate and the selected example maps the comparative construction more exactly.

held_examples.german: Tom hat immer eine Million Einfälle im Kopf.
held_examples.reason: Million is hyperbolic here; the selected example uses an explicit numeric quantity.

held_examples.german: Ich gehe in die achte Klasse.
held_examples.reason: Valid alternate; the selected example has a clear question-and-confirmation structure.

held_examples.german: Tom bat mich, sehr vorsichtig dabei zu sein.
held_examples.reason: The referent of dabei is omitted, making the sentence less self-contained than the selected example.

held_examples.german: Ich bin nicht so stark, wie ihr denkt.
held_examples.reason: Valid but comparative and context-dependent; the selected example gives a simple positive use.

held_examples.german: Was ist passiert, dass Sie so lachen müssen?
held_examples.reason: Translation adds so much; the selected example is shorter and more direct.

held_examples.german: Du hast den Nagel auf den Kopf getroffen.
held_examples.reason: The idiom means to get something exactly right, not to hit or strike a physical target.

held_examples.german: Tom hat den Nagel auf den Kopf getroffen.
held_examples.reason: The idiom means to get something exactly right, not to hit or strike a physical target.

held_examples.german: Hätte ich dich doch nur um Rat gefragt!
held_examples.reason: This is the past participle of fragen meaning asked, not the adjective gefragt meaning sought after or in demand.

held_examples.german: Ich hab Tom gefragt, wo er das herhat.
held_examples.reason: This is a verbal use meaning asked, not the adjective sense in demand.

held_examples.german: Ich weiß, daß ich Mist gemacht habe.
held_examples.reason: Mist means made a mistake in this idiom, not animal manure; daß is also superseded spelling.

held_examples.german: Wovon spricht Tom genau?
held_examples.reason: This is interrogative wovon (what about/of what), not the relative use referring back to a clause.

held_examples.german: Mir kam eine Idee in den Sinn.
held_examples.reason: This is an idiomatic use meaning came to mind; the editorial example will express sense as meaning/cogency more directly.

held_examples.german: Er hat sich an der linken Hand verletzt.
held_examples.reason: The sentence uses the reflexive verb sich verletzen, not the predicative adjective verletzt.

held_examples.german: Tom hat sich an der linken Hand verletzt.
held_examples.reason: The sentence uses the reflexive verb sich verletzen, not the predicative adjective verletzt.

held_examples.german: Was würdest du schätzen, wieviel das kosten wird?
held_examples.reason: Current standard spelling is wie viel (two words); the translation is also less idiomatic and overstates the money meaning.

held_examples.german: Was würdet ihr schätzen, wieviel das kosten wird?
held_examples.reason: Current standard spelling is wie viel (two words); the translation is also less idiomatic and overstates the money meaning.

editorial_examples.german: Der Ball hat das Fenster getroffen.
editorial_examples.note: Original literal example for treffen in its physical-contact sense.

editorial_examples.german: Dieser Beruf ist bei jungen Leuten sehr gefragt.
editorial_examples.english: This profession is in high demand among young people.
editorial_examples.note: Original example for the adjective meaning sought after or in demand.

editorial_examples.german: Der Mist muss noch aus dem Stall gebracht werden.
editorial_examples.english: The manure still needs to be removed from the stable.
editorial_examples.note: Original literal example for the animal-manure sense, avoiding the idiom einen Fehler machen.

editorial_examples.german: Er zog nach Berlin, wovon ich nichts wusste.
editorial_examples.english: He moved to Berlin, which I didn't know about.
editorial_examples.note: Original relative-clause example where wovon refers back to the fact of his move.

editorial_examples.english: This sentence doesn't make any sense.
editorial_examples.note: Original example for Sinn as meaning or intelligibility.
Original predicative adjective example; Duden gives the pattern er ist verletzt.

editorial_examples.german: Was schätzt du, wie viel die Reparatur kostet?
editorial_examples.english: How much do you think the repair will cost?
editorial_examples.note: Original present-tense example for estimating an amount; current spelling separates wie viel.

plural_reviews.note: The weak masculine noun Kunde forms its plural with -n: Kunden.

Substantivized adjective; the plural form varies with declension and determiner. Both Weiße (strong/without article) and Weißen (weak/with definite article) occur; avoid presenting these as invariant noun endings.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Substantivized adjective with variable gender and adjective declension. Plural forms include Weiße without a determiner and die Weißen with the definite article; refer to people using respectful, context-appropriate wording.

plural_reviews.note: Karten names the card game in this entry; the individual playing card is a Karte, a different sense.
plural_reviews.usage_note: In the card-game sense, Karten is used as a plural-only noun; Karte refers to an individual card.

plural_reviews.note: Duden lists Streite as the plural and marks it rare.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Rare plural. Streit is normally used as a singular abstract noun; use Auseinandersetzungen for ordinary countable disputes.

plural_reviews.note: Duden lists both plural forms Labors and Labore.
Duden lists Gäste as the plural of Gast.
For the sleep-place sense, Duden gives the plural Lager. Läger belongs to the commercial-storage sense.
plural_reviews.usage_note: In the sleep-place sense, use Lager. Läger is a business-language variant for storage depots, not this sense.

plural_reviews.note: The plural Gänge is the form for this masculine noun sense.

plural_reviews.value: No plural in the right-hand/side sense
plural_reviews.note: Rechte means the (right) hand/side here; the lexical item is normally singular. For plural hands use Hände, or use the phrase rechte Hände; the candidate declensions Rechte/Rechten do not represent this sense’s noun plural.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Die Rechte can mean the right hand and is normally singular. The plural of Hand is Hände; say rechte Hände when counting hands.

plural_reviews.value: No plural in the broadcast-medium sense
plural_reviews.note: Duden marks the broadcast-medium sense without plural; radios is the plural of the physical radio receiver.
plural_reviews.usage_note: For radio as a medium or broadcast, use the singular. Physical radio receivers pluralize as Radios.

plural_reviews.note: Duden lists both Tests and Teste; Tests is the usual contemporary form.
The strong plural of Fass is Fässer.
Knie has an unchanged nominative plural.
Duden lists Schutze and Schütze as rare plural forms, particularly in Swiss usage; the abstract protection sense is normally singular.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Rare plural forms Schutze/Schütze occur, especially in Swiss usage. For ordinary abstract protection, Schutz is generally singular; technical contexts often use Schutzvorrichtungen for countable devices.

plural_reviews.note: Roma is the plural form used for members of the Roma people; the entry’s singular Rom is masculine.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Plural Roma; use community-preferred names and wording in context.

plural_reviews.note: Duden permits these sortal plurals in technical use when distinguishing varieties; ordinary milk as a substance is generally singular.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Usually singular for milk as a substance. Fachsprachlich Milche/Milchen can distinguish varieties or types.

plural_reviews.note: Schulden is the normal plural form for debts/liabilities; this entry does not teach the separate singular Schuld meaning guilt or an individual obligation.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Plural-only in this financial-liabilities sense. Schuld can be used separately for guilt or an individual obligation.

plural_reviews.note: Monde is the plural for the moon and other natural satellites.
Daten is the plural of Datum when it means pieces of information; the singular lemma is Datum.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Plural-only in this information sense; one item is ein Datum, several are Daten.

plural_reviews.note: Siege is the regular plural of victory.
